issues.legal_issue: An amendment expressly given retrospective effect must be applied according to its plain terms even when it was enacted on an erroneous view of the law.
material_facts: The legislature enacted an amendment expressly deemed effective from an earlier date.
The amendment changed the requirements governing publication of land acquisition notifications.
The acquiring authority argued that the amendment should not apply retrospectively because the legislature had enacted it on an assumption about the law that was later rejected.
issues.conclusion: The amendment must be given retrospective effect according to its plain terms; the asserted legislative assumption does not make it prospective or superfluous.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 1(3) and 2 of the Land Acquisition (Andhra Pradesh Amendment and Validation) Act, 1983, the amendment was expressly deemed to have come into force from 12 September 1975, and its plain terms had to be applied. The court rejected the proposed limitation of its retrospective operation because the amendment did not exclude the provision it changed.

predicates.acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the validity of notifications issued as part of a land acquisition.
predicates.amendment_enacted: The legislature enacted an amendment changing requirements applicable to the acquisition notifications.
predicates.amendment_expressly_retroactive: The amendment expressly states that it takes effect from an earlier date.

issues.definition: When an acquisition proceeding concerns notifications covered by an expressly retrospective amendment, the amendment applies to those notifications.

issues.legal_issue: A land acquisition notification is invalid when local notice of its substance is given later than the maximum interval that applies between Gazette publication and local notice.
material_facts: The acquisition notification was published in the official gazette on 4 August 1977.
Notice of the substance of the notification was given in the locality on 3 October 1977, more than forty days after gazette publication.
A later notification declared the remaining land needed for the acquisition, and the landowners challenged both notifications.
The amendment imposing the maximum interval was expressly retrospective and applied to the acquisition notification.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition notification was invalid because local notice was given outside the required interval; the later notification also failed, and the decision quashing both notifications was sustained.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as amended by Sections 1(3) and 2 of the Land Acquisition (Andhra Pradesh Amendment and Validation) Act, 1983, required local notice within forty days of Gazette publication and applied retrospectively to covered notifications. A breach introduced a fatal infirmity. This is consistent with Deepak Pahwa v. Lt. Governor, Delhi, (1984) 4 SCC 308: the two steps need not be simultaneous, but a large gap may indicate a break in continuity; the amendment legislatively fixes the limit beyond which that break is presumed. The later notification could not stand once the foundational acquisition notification was invalidated.

rule.if: acquisition_proceeding and gazette_publication_made and local_notice_given and notification_covered_by_retroactive_requirement and notice_gap_exceeded_limit

predicates.acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the validity of notifications issued as part of a land acquisition.
predicates.gazette_publication_made: The acquiring authority published the acquisition notification in the official gazette.
predicates.local_notice_given: The acquiring authority gave local notice of the substance of the acquisition notification.
predicates.notification_covered_by_retroactive_requ: The acquisition notification was issued within the period to which the retrospectively effective requirement applies.
predicates.notice_gap_exceeded_limit: The interval between gazette publication and local notice exceeded the maximum interval required by the applicable rule.

issues.definition: If a covered acquisition notification is followed by local notice after the maximum permitted interval, the acquisition notifications are invalid.
